evals.prompt: We have three scenarios for the battery market — what early-warning indicators would tell us which one is unfolding, and are they actually diagnostic?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Takes the three scenarios as given rather than rebuilding them; Generates observable, dated, thresholded candidate indicators per scenario; Rates every indicator against every scenario on the HL/L/C/U/HU scale and computes spread; Drops indicators that would appear under all scenarios and reports per-scenario coverage; Returns a monitoring plan with source, threshold, cadence and owner per kept indicator.
expectations: Takes the three scenarios as given rather than rebuilding them
Generates observable, dated, thresholded candidate indicators per scenario
Rates every indicator against every scenario on the HL/L/C/U/HU scale and computes spread
Drops indicators that would appear under all scenarios and reports per-scenario coverage
Returns a monitoring plan with source, threshold, cadence and owner per kept indicator

evals.prompt: Validate our indicator list: here are 14 signposts our team wrote for the four futures in last quarter's scenario exercise. Which ones actually discriminate between the futures and which are noise?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Builds the Indicators Validator matrix (indicators x scenarios); Computes diagnosticity (spread) per indicator and gives keep / weak / drop verdicts; Flags scenarios with fewer than three unique indicators and asks for more; Uses scripts/indicators.py or reproduces its arithmetic by hand.
expectations: Builds the Indicators Validator matrix (indicators x scenarios)
Computes diagnosticity (spread) per indicator and gives keep / weak / drop verdicts
Flags scenarios with fewer than three unique indicators and asks for more
Uses scripts/indicators.py or reproduces its arithmetic by hand

evals.prompt: Build a signpost list for our scenario set on European data-centre power demand so we know which scenario is playing out — with owners and a review cadence.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Generates 5-15 candidate indicators per scenario meeting the five qualities (observable, valid, reliable, stable, unique); Validates them against all scenarios and keeps the diagnostic set; Emits the output template: matrix, dropped list, coverage, monitoring plan, absence rule, re-validation date.
expectations: Generates 5-15 candidate indicators per scenario meeting the five qualities (observable, valid, reliable, stable, unique)
Validates them against all scenarios and keeps the diagnostic set
Emits the output template: matrix, dropped list, coverage, monitoring plan, absence rule, re-validation date

evals.prompt: Our watchlist keeps 'confirming' every scenario at the same time. Can you check which of these indicators are diagnostic and set up a proper monitoring plan?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Diagnoses the problem as non-diagnostic indicators (likely under every scenario); Rates each indicator against each scenario and drops uniform rows; Produces a monitoring plan with sources, thresholds, cadence, owners and a re-validation date.
expectations: Diagnoses the problem as non-diagnostic indicators (likely under every scenario)
Rates each indicator against each scenario and drops uniform rows
Produces a monitoring plan with sources, thresholds, cadence, owners and a re-validation date

evals.prompt: Help us build 2x2 scenarios for the future of the European battery market over the next five years — what are the critical uncertainties and the plausible futures?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Does not start from an existing scenario set or rate indicators; Runs scenario planning: driving forces, critical uncertainties, 2x2 matrix, narrated futures.
expectations: Does not start from an existing scenario set or rate indicators
Runs scenario planning: driving forces, critical uncertainties, 2x2 matrix, narrated futures

evals.prompt: Do a quick scan for weak signals at the fringe of the grid-storage industry — what is emerging that nobody is watching yet?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Does not presuppose scenarios or build a validator matrix; Runs a horizon-scanning sweep: signal log with sources, clustering into issues, scored radar.
expectations: Does not presuppose scenarios or build a validator matrix
Runs a horizon-scanning sweep: signal log with sources, clustering into issues, scored radar

evals.prompt: When will sodium-ion cells reach cost parity with LFP for stationary storage? Give me a dated prediction with kill-signals and a review date.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Does not build a multi-scenario indicator matrix; Produces one dated prediction with accelerants, blockers, weak signals, kill-signals and a review date (foresight behaviour).
expectations: Does not build a multi-scenario indicator matrix
Produces one dated prediction with accelerants, blockers, weak signals, kill-signals and a review date (foresight behaviour)
